      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Add a message parameter to reachability checks so failure messages are more verbose",
      "quote": "I think it'd be great to add a message to this, so failures are more verbose.",

      "other_replies": [],

      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Provide multiple reachability functions for different condition types where comparison parameters are passed directly",
      "quote": "It could also make sense to provide multiple reachability functions for different condition types, where the parameters of the comparison are passed directly",

      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "dergoegge agreed this can be added later",

      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Whether the deserialization in partially_downloaded_block is a good candidate for a reachability goal",
      "quote": "Is this deserialization a good candidate for it?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained why it was used and that explicit goal registration was needed",
      "author_replies": ["rc:3881622776"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3881622776",
      "status_by_quote": "right, but currently the Goal is registered while `ReachabilityGoal()` is called at the first time."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3893852415",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "The validation_load_mempool check could pass trivially on empty files without verifying that mempool features like unbroadcast sets and fee deltas were loaded",
      "quote": "Instead of a plain \"success\" (which probably happens on an empty file), it may be better to ensure all features are covered",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "maflcko pointed out that the commit still contained the unaddressed check",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4035006114", "rc:4063086838"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4259912989",
      "status_by_quote": "I don't think it was. I still see 56a89c4e1d88ad34016d4ac8fe7ccfd51c9972ad"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3923910367",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Why buffer to std::cerr if the check passed",
      "quote": "Why buffer to `std::cerr` if it may have passed?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "Crypt-iQ noted sending passing output to std::cout is minor",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4063204536"],
      "other_replies": ["rc:4063363226"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4084074457",
      "status_by_quote": "I meant that it could go to `std::cout` instead if it passed, but it's pretty minor."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3923944702",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Using std::_Exit circumvents normal destruction and resource cleanup on exit",
      "quote": "Why `std::_Exit` which according to https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/utility/program/_Exit does not clean up resources compared to `std::exit`?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "Crypt-iQ accepted that returning a non-zero exit code via std::_Exit is correct",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": ["rc:4033542005"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4037107551",
      "status_by_quote": "Ah, ok. I was assuming that you'd know if it error'd from stderr, but returning non-zero exit code is correct."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3926290032",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Whether reachability checks are intended for a static corpus CI job rather than active fuzzing",
      "quote": "I guess the purpose of the reachability checks (without the fuzzing guidance mentioned in a thread above) is for a CI job running a static corpus + detecting regressions (i.e. not  fuzzing)?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "maflcko confirmed it is intended for a nightly CI job on static corpora with -runs=1",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": ["rc:4033535571"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4033535571",
      "status_by_quote": "Yes, mostly for a nightly CI job on a static corpora folder with `-runs=1`."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4096766881",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Consider whether some failure cases could also be reachability goals",

      "author_replies": [],

      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Some reachability goals cannot be reached when process_message is executed with LIMIT_TO_MESSAGE_TYPE",
      "quote": "I think some goals can't be reached if this target is running with `LIMIT_TO_MESSAGE_TYPE` (ofc depending on the message).",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "maflcko replied that LIMIT_TO_MESSAGE_TYPE and FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY are expected to be mutually exclusive",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": ["rc:4259675850"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4259675850",
      "status_by_quote": "I'd say it is expected that LIMIT_TO_MESSAGE_TYPE=... and FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1 are mutually exclusive."
    },

      "kind": "correctness",

      "author_replies": [],
